parsed_response.citation_summary: International et al. (Year). Global analysis of pollination, cocoa tree, plantation, and climate factors affecting cocoa yield. Experimental data from Brazil, Ghana, and Indonesia. Key findings: hand-pollination increases yield by 20%; soil resources (leaf litter, large trees) increase yield by 9-19%; 7°C cooler temperatures during hot season increase yield by up to 31%.

mechanisms.description: Pollinator limitation constrains cocoa yield; hand-pollination bypasses natural pollination constraints, directly increasing fruit set and yield
Soil resources (organic matter from leaf litter, root access from larger trees) improve nutrient and water availability, supporting higher plant productivity
High temperatures during hot seasons stress cocoa plants; temperature reduction decreases heat stress, improving physiological function and yield

parsed_response.methodology: Experimental study using hand-pollination interventions across three major cocoa-producing countries (Brazil, Ghana, Indonesia) to test pollination limitation, soil resource effects, and temperature effects on cocoa yield. The study compares yields under hand-pollination conditions versus natural pollination, and under different temperature conditions.
